items.body:
## Disposition: closing this overlapping umbrella request

I should have checked the existing reports before opening this issue. The fail-closed tool-policy requirement is already tracked in #41979; pre-render response holding is tracked in #43254. #54806 independently reports trusted hook discovery without effective Desktop interception on the same Windows backend version, including control-socket error 10050. #54427 tracks trusted resolved execution context, and #54872 covers cancellation-driven policy-gate waiting.

This report combined those requirements rather than isolating a demonstrated new defect. Closing in favor of the established reports. The local failed control is retained below as bounded evidence; its cause is unknown and it does not prove the same root cause as #54806. No working live-enforcement solution or maintainer acceptance is claimed. Any remaining user-conversation role-binding gap needs a separate novelty check before another report.

---

# Required native alignment admission is unavailable; hook failures cannot establish mandatory enforcement

For OpenAI Codex desktop/native runtime maintainers. Submitted with the reporter’s authorization.

## Requested outcome

Provide a host-owned, mandatory admission boundary before native actions and final rendering. The client needs to reject an action when required authority or a valid policy decision is unavailable. Optional repository adapters and additional prompt instructions cannot intercept paths that bypass them.

This request concerns deterministic action-policy enforcement. Delivery of instruction bytes does not prove that a model followed every instruction or reasoned correctly.

## Environment

- Windows; running desktop backend reports `codex-cli 0.163.0-alpha.10.2`.
- The PATH CLI reports `0.149.1`; it was not used for the fresh native probe.
- Node 24 with native TypeScript stripping. The intercepted probe target is the read-only local function `get_goal({})`, not a shell action.
- Probe runtime home, state, logs and temporary output are isolated beneath a repository-owned temporary fixture. Native turn context records approval `never` and sandbox `read-only`. This is configuration/path isolation, not a claim of OS-enforced confinement.

## Fresh observation, 2026-10-20

1. Discover a session-only `PreToolUse` command hook matching exactly `^get_goal$`.
2. Use only the host-returned hook key/hash to configure trust for the isolated child session.
3. Verify that the expected hook is trusted and enabled, with no other active trusted handler.
4. Emit exactly one `get_goal({})` call through a local deterministic Responses responder.
5. The native tool returns `goal: null`, but no matching hook-execution receipt is recorded. The control fails. Denial and failure cases are not run afterward.

The cause of this fresh missing receipt is not established. This result is not evidence of successful denial, successful interception, or current-chat enforcement.

A separate read-only attempt to connect to the existing app-server control socket failed with Windows socket error 10050. It created no thread and performed no configuration write. It does not establish that every possible host transport is unavailable.

## Prior bounded observations, 2026-10-19

A separately preserved assessment of the desktop backend version used the same non-shell target and matched native call/output records to hook receipts. A valid explicit denial blocked the call. Controlled exit 1, malformed hook output and timeout each allowed the call. These historical results have not been relabeled as fresh passing tests.

A custom Responses gateway separately withheld synthetic tool-call frames on negative/missing/invalid checks and gateway failures. That demonstrates only calls routed through that fixture gateway. No production upstream proxy, mandatory current-chat routing or global mediation was established.

## Documented constraints

[Official hook documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks) describes supported explicit denial, callback failures that can leave actions unblocked, incomplete tool-path coverage, and exceptions to the ordinary hook path. [Plugin documentation](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins) also requires separate trust for plugin hooks. Installing a plugin or catching errors inside a hook does not establish host-owned mandatory mediation.

## Smallest host-owned repair requested

1. Add an explicit required-policy admission contract, separate from ordinary advisory hooks. This is a proposed capability, not an existing setting.
2. Bind admission to the actual thread, turn, original outcome, exact operation/payload, authority revision and single-use request identity.
3. Enforce it at every relevant native dispatch path, including nested code-mode calls. Unsupported paths must be exposed and denied when required by policy, rather than silently bypassing admission.
4. Deny on missing/untrusted/modified authority, missing checker, launcher failure, checker crash, invalid response, deadline expiry or lost policy transport.
5. Apply the corresponding original-outcome gate before final bytes are rendered. Uncertain continuation effects must remain reserved across restart and require authoritative reconciliation.
6. Expose authenticated invocation/decision observations and a supported way to bind the current conversation. Caller-created environment secrets, local brands and authored JSON must not qualify as production host evidence.

Existing repository adapters already exercise sealed role/skill bodies, exact byte binding, issued guards, durable duplicate suppression and uncertain-effect reconciliation. They can be integration targets, but cannot establish their own mandatory invocation.

## Acceptance tests

- A positive exact-bound admission executes one harmless action once.
- Explicit denial and every unavailable/error path execute zero actions.
- Wrong-thread, wrong-turn, changed payload, changed authority, replay and expired admission are denied.
- Nested/local/MCP/subagent paths cannot bypass the required boundary; unsupported hosted paths are explicitly identified.
- An unfinished original outcome cannot release final bytes; continuation is acknowledged and duplicate-safe.
- Restart preserves reservations and original-parent identity.
- Tests inspect native dispatch and rendered-output evidence, not simulated assistant prose alone.

## Safety and disclosure

Persistent configuration, execution policy, signing-service/trust-authority work and native Stop enablement were excluded. Hashes of the three named configuration files match before/after the fresh probe; this is not a whole-host mutation audit. No production guard was installed. Private prompts, account information, credentials and conversation identifiers are intentionally excluded from this report.

## Separate project-hook role applicability defect

Source review found that a project-wide alignment command selected one assistant identity using only the repository working directory. Other role-specific conversations can share that directory. Matching source hashes and tests that assume a single role do not establish correct applicability. A reviewed inactive repository patch now emits only neutral workspace context and imports no role-specific memory/authority loader; it deliberately withholds role-specific context even in the intended assistant conversation until a trusted host identity exists. Prompt text, titles, transcript text, environment flags and caller-authored role fields cannot supply that identity.

Please expose a trustworthy role/session binding for user-owned conversations as well as native subagents, preserving it across resume and compaction. Optional subagent profile fields do not by themselves identify a separate user-owned conversation. This remains distinct from mandatory tool/final-render admission. No live configuration or trust change has been made.
